title: They start excellent, but after a couple of washes they become difficult to clean.
text:
They start excellent, but after a couple of washes they become difficult to clean.. I was super excited to get these. I just received a bottle of Tennessee whiskey and when I saw these glasses I knew they would be perfect to break open my bottle with. They're a little classier than the shot glasses and whiskey glasses I have, and they look great without liquid in them too.

When I opened them out of the box, I was a little surprised to find they were made of glass. They seemed--and still seem--a little thin and almost plastic-like in feel. I'm almost confident they're glass, but it's a very thin glass. I think it would've been better if the outside was solid; instead, it's just a thin, single wall around the glass and the bottom is completely open. It's cheaper for them to make, but difficult for us to clean. As we don't have a dishwasher and I wash all my dishes by hand, I have to use both the regular dish scrub and a bottle scrub to get in all the crevices.

But the thinness of the glass starts to rear its deformed head after a few uses. At first I thought it was me, but when my wife, who doesn't drink whiskey at all, mentioned that the glasses looked yellow I realized it just wasn't me. The glasses were staining and were not getting cleaner the more I cleaned them. They look great when there's liquid in them, but on the cupboard they don't look attractive. The outside would've been better if it was solid glass rather than a thin wall, methinks.

It's a shame because I think the design is really neat and I they work mostly great. The rim, I think, could be a bit thinner as sometimes the liquid has too much space to travel on top of the glass before it reaches the inside of my mouth, so sometimes the liquid unintentionally slips over the edge of my lips.
